shared_elements: low-relief figural carving on an upright slab/pillar
row of repeated arch- or loop-shaped motifs across the upper zone
horizontal dividing band with a fringe/row of short strokes
schematic creature with a rounded head shown in relief
paired symmetrical motifs flanking a central axis
arms/limbs rendered as thin raised bands ending in hands or claws
justification: Both surfaces are upright slabs bearing shallow, strongly schematic relief organised into stacked registers: a row of repeated arch-like motifs across the top, a horizontal band with a comb/fringe of short strokes beneath it, and below that rounded-headed creatures whose thin band-like arms converge toward a central point, plus a disc/boss element. The biggest difference is that A is itself carved as a single colossal anthropomorphic body (head, shoulders, belted torso, hands on the belly), so its motifs are worn as attributes on a figure, whereas B is a flat panel presenting several small independent creatures side by side with no overarching body form.
